wgo: **Intro** Start with a guitar pick up octave line brings the band in on I **Rhythm Section:** The rhythm section locks into a steady, floating groove based on the I chord. **Verse (12-Bar Cycle)** - **Bars 1-4:** Alternate between Emaj7 for two bars and C#m7 for two bars. - **Bars 5-8:** Repeat the same pattern: Emaj7 followed by C#m7. - **Bars 9-10:** Move to the minor chord, F#m7, for two bars. - **Bars 11-12:** Set up with the A/B chord for the turnaround, lasting two bars. **Pre-Chorus ("Picket lines...")** - **Chords:** Use F#m7 for two bars, followed by A/B for another two bars. - **Dynamics:** Slightly intensify the energy here to create momentum leading into the chorus. **Chorus ("You know we've got to find a way...")** - **Chords:** Keep the same chord structure as the verse (Emaj7 and C#m7), but now change the chords twice as fast-one bar each instead of two. **Vamp / Interlude** - **Chords:** Transition to Am9 (or A minor) groove. - **Cue:** While the bass and percussion maintain a steady pulse - This vamp or interlude solo section repeats twice. Following the interlude, there's a direct transition into "Mercy Mercy Me." **The 1-6-2-5 "Mercy" Loop (3 Verses & Riff)** - **Chords:** Each chord gets two full bars: - Emaj7 (2 bars) - the I chord - C#m7 (2 bars) - the vi7 chord - F#m7 (2 bars) - the ii7 chord - B7 or B13 (2 bars) - the V7 chord (or you can use A/B instead) After playing through three verses of "Mercy Me," transition back into the "What's Going On" interlude, which ends on the I chord (Emaj7).

hush: After the guitar solo in "Hard to Handle," the music smoothly transitions into the intro of Deep Purple's "Hush," while still staying in the same key. The structure follows this sequence: intro, verse, chorus, verse, chorus, solo, and wraps up with a final half-time section. You'll hear the recognizable hook: "NaNa Na Na Na Na Na Na Na Na ." The band then hits a hard stop on the I chord, leaving the vocals to shine alone with, "Hey little thing, let me light your candle 'cause... I'm so hard to handle now..." band joins back in to finish with the standard 3 Tag ending of "Hard to Handle."
